title: Reward what you want
summary: Evolution gives you exactly what you pay for. Pay for the wrong thing and runners learn the wrong thing.

steps.title: Paid to stand around
steps.body:
This script pays a tenth of a point for every tick a runner is still going. It sounds harmless: runners that last longer must be doing well.

Press Check. It trains 40 runners for 8 generations, one course each, and reports the share of courses the best fifth of them finished.

They hardly finish. Crossing the line ends the run and stops the points, so the best scorers learn to wander until the clock runs out. Pay for new ground and the finish instead.

check.message: The best fifth should finish more than half of their courses.

hints: Remove reward +0.1. Pay for agent.progressGain and agent.finished, as in the first lesson.
Write reward +10 * agent.progressGain and reward +10 when agent.finished.

steps.title: Stop runners that give up
steps.body:
A runner stuck behind a crate wastes time. The room ends a run after 4 seconds without new ground, but you can be stricter.

`agent.stuckTime` counts the seconds since the runner last got closer. Add `stop "stuck" when agent.stuckTime > 2 s`. Runners that dither now lose their run sooner, and generations finish faster.

check.message: Add a stop rule that reads agent.stuckTime.

hints: A stop rule looks like stop "reason" when condition.

steps.title: Time to spare
steps.body:
Two runners that both finish score the same, even if one took twice as long. Pay a little for speed.

`agent.timeLeft` is the seconds left on the clock. Units keep numbers honest: seconds cannot be added to points, so divide by `1 s` to get a plain number. Add `reward +0.5 * agent.timeLeft / 1 s when agent.finished`.

check.message: The test run should score more than 22 points.

hints: The bonus only counts on the tick the runner finishes, so end it with when agent.finished.
Write reward +0.5 * agent.timeLeft / 1 s when agent.finished.
